task_set.title: Bigville offline retrieval set
task_set.provenance: Expected files were selected by reading Bigville implementations and focused tests in the read-only checkout. These frozen labels are supplied to Ozagia; the evaluator never imports Bigville.

arm_descriptions.baseline: Plain source-file listing, sorted by path, truncated to budget.
arm_descriptions.dev_context: DevMemory.context items/snippets, executed at the budget.
arm_descriptions.dev_repo_map: Ranked repo map, executed at the budget.
arm_descriptions.both: Union of the dev_context and dev_repo_map file sets.
arm_descriptions.grep: Lexical baseline: files ranked by distinct task terms found in their text, then total occurrences, then path.
arm_descriptions.code_search: ozagia.core.search.code_search results, rendered as path:line: snippet in result order, truncated to budget.

tasks.task: Saving and restoring a running session should preserve enough state to continue the same simulation after restart.
tasks.notes: Session checkpoint implementation and focused roundtrip tests.

tasks.task: Repeated population summaries with the same sampling seed should report stable estimates and uncertainty while retaining exact counts.
tasks.notes: Reporting computes exact values and seeded finite population sample estimates.

tasks.task: Large action menus should be generated on demand when the configured automatic mode detects that eager enumeration is too costly.
tasks.notes: Mode resolution lives in Game; lazy evaluation behavior has dedicated tests.

tasks.task: When concurrent actions claim the same scarce item, resolution should choose a deterministic winner and leave conflicting claims rejected.
tasks.notes: Pure claim arbitration and its executor tests are the relevant implementation and validation sites.

tasks.task: Restoring a saved knowledge graph should preserve loaded seed manifests and reject malformed manifest data instead of silently losing it.
tasks.notes: Graph checkpoint encoding and seed manifest validation are implemented in runtime; node provenance tests cover loaded origins.

tasks.task: All cognition providers should submit decisions through one shared contract so a provider cannot bypass the world's action checks.
tasks.notes: Backend interface, game decision loop, and backend contract tests.

tasks.task: Scenario loading should accept structured in memory definitions and file paths while producing a clear validation failure for malformed input.
tasks.notes: Scenario loader and scenario validation suite.

tasks.task: The public entry point should build a game from a selected scenario and seed while keeping provider and runtime choices configurable.
tasks.notes: Public API construction and defaults tests.

`tests/test_engine_defaults.py` | Public API construction and defaults tests. | ## Reading these numbers - This is a **retrieval instrument**, not an end-to-end coding benchmark: it measures whether known-relevant files are selected, not whether an agent completes a change. - `baseline` is a sorted-path file-listing control, not a semantic retriever. `grep` is a lexical control: it counts distinct task words found in each file's text. - `recall` counts a hit at any tier. `recall_content` counts only hits whose file the arm showed as code (code_search snippet, dev_context item with snippet text, or repo-map `full`/`outline` tier). A listing-tier hit tells the reader the path exists, not what it contains. - Token estimates are each module's own ~4-chars/token heuristic. Cache counts apply only to repo-map arms. - `both` is the literal union of the two retrievers run at the same budget; its token cost and latency are the sum of the components, so its budget is per component (up to 2x the nominal budget). Compare it as a cost/recall trade-off, not as an equal-token arm. - `code_search` runs once per task; its elapsed time is the same call's time at every budget. - Ground truth is frozen in the task JSON. Re-run the scoped tests after moving or renaming an expected file.
